facts: The oracle first calls OpenSearchLogIndexBootstrap.ensureInstalled twice with a fixed Clock and the same caller-owned OpenSearchClient, then constructs OpenSearchLogIndex(OpenSearchClient, RetentionInstallation.activeIndex()).

Bootstrap observations use the returned identities plus ISM explain, policy GET, template/mapping reads, and exact-index existence; direct client document indexing or querying remains outside the data-plane proof.

The exact resources are policy log-debug-retention-v1, template log-debug-v1-template, and fixed-clock UTC index log-debug-v1-YYYY.MM.dd. Both bootstrap calls must converge on these identities without duplicate or wildcard resources.

The active index must be ISM-managed by the named policy whose terminal delete action has min_index_age 7d, and must expose the approved v1 date, keyword identity/correlation, and text message mapping before the IndexPort round trip.
RunIdLogQuery requires an exact non-blank testRunId, a required half-open TimeWindow, maxRecords from 1 through 200, and an optional conjunctive message term; it never broadens to workload fallback.

WorkloadWindowLogQuery requires non-blank namespace and workload plus the required half-open interval, maxRecords from 1 through 200, and an optional conjunctive message term; every returned record must satisfy all identity and time predicates.

LogQueryResult contains sanitized NormalizedLogRecord values and a truncated flag; the three current conditions prove named-field round trip, exact run-id isolation, and the namespace/workload/time conjunction without adding a separate pagination surface.

The proof must use an authorized ephemeral real OpenSearch instance. A disconnected Docker-compatible runtime or absent configured endpoint is an environment checkpoint and cannot be replaced by an in-memory fake or claimed as behavioral red/green.

This feature owns only the independent real-store contract oracle and fixtures. Adapter/bootstrap implementation, canonical resources, Maven dependency, and adapter tests remain feat-004; MCP behavior remains feat-006/007 and Kubernetes lifecycle remains feat-011.
